title: Question 4
stem:
A spring is supported so that it hangs vertically, as shown in Fig. 4.1.
Different masses are attached to the lower end of the spring. The extension x of the spring is measured for each mass M. The variation with x of M is shown in Fig. 4.2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State and explain whether the spring obeys Hooke’s law.

markscheme_points.text: the straight line does not go through the origin/the force is not proportional to extension (so does not obey Hooke’s law)

hints: Hint 1: Consider the physical mechanism underlying this process based on physical principles and measurement.
parts.proper_answer: the straight line does not go through the origin/the force is not proportional to extension (so does not obey Hooke’s law)

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Calculate the work done on the spring as it is extended from x = 40.0 mm to x = 160 mm.
$\text{work done} = J$

markscheme_points.text: work done is represented by/linked to area under the line (× g)

hints: Hint 1: Identify the given data from the problem and recall the governing equation connecting these quantities using physical principles and measurement.
Hint 2: Rearrange the formula to isolate the required quantity before substituting numerical values with correct powers of ten.
Hint 3: Check your intermediate calculation steps carefully and ensure your final answer is stated to an appropriate number of significant figures with correct SI units.
parts.proper_answer: work done is represented by/linked to area under the line (× g); work = ½ (145 + 70) × 10-3 × 9.81 × 120 × 10-3; = 0.13 (0.127) J
